children: GE Vernova T&D India shares jumped nearly 8 percent in early trade on Tuesday after brokerages issued bullish calls post a major HVDC project that may be worth Rs 13,000 crore, and could materially lift the company's earnings over the coming years. The power transmission equipment maker’s stock rose 7.6 percent to around Rs 4,700 in early trade, making it the top gainer on the midcap index. GE Vernova T&D India shares had closed 1.4 percent higher at Rs 4,367.2 on Monday.

The latest surge takes the stock’s gains so far in 2026 to around 48 percent, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which is down around 9 percent over the same period. The company’s market capitalisation stood at around Rs 1.12 lakh crore based on Monday’s close.

Nomura retained its ‘buy’ rating on GE Vernova T&D India and raised its target price to Rs 6,000 per share, implying around 37 percent upside from Monday’s closing price. The brokerage described the company’s estimated Rs 13,000-crore HVDC order as a landmark win that enhances its long-term growth outlook.

Nomura now expects GE Vernova T&D India’s profit after tax to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 31 percent over FY26-FY29. It also raised its FY28 and FY29 revenue estimates by 4 percent and 9 percent, respectively. Nomura said that the stock was trading at 39 times its FY29 earnings estimate of Rs 111 per share.

Citi sees 25% boost to FY29 earnings

Citi also maintained its ‘buy’ call on GE Vernova T&D India, with a target price of Rs 5,400 per share. The brokerage said the company had won Power Grid’s 800 kV HVDC LCC project for the Barmer II-South Kalamb transmission corridor. Revenue recognition is expected to begin from FY29, with Citi estimating that the project could lift its FY29 EBITDA and earnings per share estimates by around 25 percent.

Citi said that Hitachi Energy India had previously been expected to secure the project, given its higher local content and execution bandwidth. The brokerage maintained a ‘buy’ rating on Hitachi Energy India but cut its target price to Rs 42,000 per share.
GE Vernova emerges L1 bidder for Power Grid project

GE Vernova T&D India said on Monday that it had emerged as the lowest bidder, or L1 bidder, for a Power Grid Corporation of India project to establish a 6,000 MW, 800 kV high-voltage direct-current transmission system. The project involves two 3,000 MW terminal stations at Barmer II in Rajasthan and South Kalamb in Maharashtra using line-commutated converter technology. GE Vernova T&D India will undertake the design, supply and execution of the project, which will be implemented over multiple years.

The transmission corridor is intended to evacuate renewable power from Rajasthan and forms part of India’s expansion of high-capacity transmission infrastructure. While GE Vernova did not disclose the contract value in its exchange filing, Nomura estimates the order at around Rs 13,000 crore.
